title: Precious Practice
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett leads a guided reflection on how rare and precious it is to practice together, using a Tibetan-style visualization of people who cannot practice because of illness, disability, poverty, or war, and of the founding teachers Suzuki Roshi and Katagiri Roshi in 1950s America. Nomon then reads from Suzuki Roshi's 1961 remarks, later titled "Teacher and Disciple," on emptiness, the unbroken effort between practice and enlightenment, and the Yakusan story of the Zen master who asks to be acknowledged. Along the way, Nomon recalls a quiet day with Norman Fischer making calligraphy on a rakusu, after which a sister-in-law says "you really seem different." Nomon closes with Dogen's line that everyone is your teacher, and the habit of hurry.
